entries.subject: A colour for Epsilon Indi Bb
entries.finding: The only resolved spectra of Epsilon Indi Bb, from King et al. (2010, A&A 510, A99; VizieR J/A+A/510/A99), are flux-calibrated but start at 630 nm. The missing 380 to 630 nm carries most of what the eye would see: with the gap filled by a ramp through the resolved V limit it holds 63% of the luminance, and the colour moves from sRGB (255, 0, 0) with the gap empty to about (255, 42, 0) with it filled, so a colour would be the fill, not a measurement. A blackbody at the temperature would misrepresent a brown dwarf's absorbed spectrum as well. It stays the shared neutral gray. Model spectra were tested on 2026-09-28 against Luhman 16 A, a dwarf of nearly the same temperature whose optical colour is measured (#ff2f96): the cloud-free Sonora Bobcat spectra (Marley et al. 2021) give violet (#7800ff) and the cloudy Sonora Diamondback fit to Luhman 16 of Mader et al. (2026) gives red (#ff656a), 54 levels from the measurement where two colours of one star may differ by 12; no cloudy-model fit of Epsilon Indi B is published to choose its clouds by. Below 1,000 K the Planck colour is refused as well.
entries.revisitWhen: A flux-calibrated spectrum of the resolved component covering about 400 to 630 nm is published.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The limb is drawn on the colour lens, which this dwarf does not have. PICASO 4.1 on the Sonora Bobcat atmospheres gives a V-band law at its temperature and gravity (node packages/telescope-cli/src/new-object/new-object-cli.mts --star-limb), but from the same cloud-free models whose visible spectrum fails the Luhman 16 A test above, and there is no colour to draw it on. No law is published for this dwarf.
entries.revisitWhen: The colour entry is resolved, or a limb law is published for this dwarf.
